one_liner: Batch image-resize CLI, C++ library and Ruby gem that claims 1.7-2.9x over the libvips CLI on an Apple M2.
what_it_does: Decodes a JPEG, PNG, WebP or BMP file, resizes it (fit width, fit height, exact size or scale) and re-encodes it, either one file at a time or as a batch over a directory or file list on a thread pool. The C++ API is file-path based (fastresize::resize, resize_with_format, batch_resize, batch_resize_custom with ResizeOptions and BatchOptions); there is no in-memory buffer API in include/fastresize.h. The same core is exposed as the fast_resize CLI and a Ruby gem. It is not a drop-in for libvips or imageflow: there are no other operations, no colour management and no metadata or EXIF handling (auto-rotate is an open request, issue #3).
how_it_is_fast: Most of the speed comes from doing less work per image: on ARM64 any downscale with the default Mitchell (or triangle) filter is rerouted to the repo's own kernels in src/simd_resize.cpp, a 2-tap fixed-point bilinear for ratios up to 3x and an integer box/area average above 3x, instead of the requested Mitchell filter. JPEG decode uses libjpeg-turbo with DCT-domain shrink-on-load (scale 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 when the integer ratio allows), JDCT_IFAST and do_fancy_upsampling = FALSE, and JPEG encode also uses JDCT_IFAST. Files are read through mmap, and batches run on a thread pool sized 1/2/4/8 by batch size (8 for 50 or more files; docs/API.md says 0 means auto-detect CPU cores, but the code does not query the core count), or a 4/8/4 decode/resize/encode pipeline when max_speed is set. On x86 the custom kernels do not exist (simd_resize returns false), so resizing there is plain stb_image_resize2 with its own SSE2/AVX code, despite the README's 'SSE2/AVX (x86)' wording.
when_to_use: Bulk thumbnailing of RGB JPEG/BMP/WebP photos to a fixed width on Apple Silicon or other ARM64 servers, where bilinear or box quality is acceptable
Ruby or shell pipelines that want one command for decode, resize and encode of a directory, with no libvips or ImageMagick install
Large JPEG downscales (2x or more) where libjpeg-turbo DCT scaling does most of the reduction
Workloads that stay within the four supported formats and need low peak RAM per batch
when_not_to_use: RGBA input on ARM64: the 4-channel NEON bilinear path overflows int16 lanes (see gotchas), so PNG or WebP with alpha downscaled by less than 3x comes out corrupted

When resampling quality matters: the default 'Mitchell' is silently replaced by 2-tap bilinear (aliases above about 2x) or truncating box averaging on ARM, and JPEG decode and encode use the less accurate IFAST DCT without fancy chroma upsampling

Shipping the x86 build to other machines: CMakeLists.txt adds -march=native on x86_64, and issue #2 (opened by the libvips maintainer) reports the prebuilt Linux x64 binary dying with an illegal instruction on a Threadripper PRO 3955WX
Untrusted or very large inputs: issue #2 also reports a segfault on a 30,000 x 30,000 image and corrupt JPEG output from a git-master build on Ubuntu 25.10, open with no maintainer reply
When you need EXIF orientation, ICC profiles, metadata, in-memory buffers, or any operation other than resize

integration.form: static lib (default) or shared lib, plus CLI binary and Ruby gem
integration.dependencies: libjpeg-turbo, libpng (with zlib), pthreads, libwebp (optional; CMake only warns if missing); stb_image, stb_image_write and stb_image_resize2 are vendored
integration.min_toolchain: C++14, CMake 3.15+; Ruby 2.5+ for the gem
integration.platforms: macOS and Linux on arm64 (custom NEON kernels) and x86_64 (stb_image_resize2 only; release builds use -march=native)
integration.thread_safety: Batch functions are internally multi-threaded; the last-error code and message are one process-wide mutex-protected global, so concurrent callers overwrite each other's errors
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it can stand in for a 'vips resize'/'vips thumbnail' or imageflow_tool batch-resize step on JPEG/PNG/WebP/BMP files, but it has a different API and none of their other operations

gotchas: Correctness bug behind the PNG benchmark row: resize_bilinear_neon_rgba computes the 4-channel weights with vmulq_s16 and vshrq_n_s16 on 0-255 values times 8-bit weights up to 256 (products up to 65,280), which wraps signed 16-bit lanes; emulating the lane math shows any channel interpolated to 128 or more coming out as 0 in flat areas (alpha 255 becomes 0), with about 74% of random pixel quads giving wrong values. The benchmark's 2104x1160 RGBA PNGs (2.63x downscale on an M2) take exactly this path. The 3-channel path is scalar int code and is not affected.
The same NEON path loads 8 bytes per 4-byte pixel (vld1_u8) at the last column, so it reads 4 bytes past the end of the source buffer on the last row.

A default 'cmake ..' configure fails: FASTRESIZE_BUILD_TESTS and FASTRESIZE_BUILD_BENCHMARKS default ON but the tests/ and benchmark/ directories are not in the public repo, so the benchmark harness behind the published numbers is unpublished.

Batch mode writes output_dir/<input file name>, so the output format follows the input extension; for PNG output, quality 85 maps to zlib level 2 (9 - (q-1)*9/99), which is much cheaper than libvips' default PNG compression, while BENCHMARKS.md says all output was JPEG q85.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over libvips or fast_image_resize only for bulk RGB thumbnailing on ARM where a single command and low RAM matter more than filter quality; fast_image_resize gives proper convolution filters (Lanczos3, bilinear) with published single-thread numbers against libvips, and stb-image-resize-opt is the better choice if you want stb_image_resize2 itself made faster, which is all FastResize uses on x86.
verified_claims_summary: First-party only: on a MacBook Pro M2 (16 GB, macOS Sonoma), resizing 1,000 images per format to 800 px width (two runs averaged) took FastResize v1.0.0 2.10 s (JPG), 3.43 s (PNG RGBA), 1.65 s (BMP) and 14.03 s (WebP), versus 5.24/6.18/4.72/23.52 s for the libvips 8.15 vips CLI in an unstated 'parallel' arrangement and 6.60/8.41/n.a./15.69 s for imageflow_tool 2.0. No scripts, commands or compiler are published, FastResize ran bilinear/box with IFAST JPEG coding against the baselines' default higher-quality kernels, and the PNG row ran the overflowing RGBA kernel described in the gotchas.
status_note: BSD-3-Clause and small (21 commits, 2025-12-03 to 2026-01-07, 67 stars), but quiet since January 2026 with issue #2's corruption, illegal-instruction and segfault reports unanswered, so treat it as an unvetted single-author project and fix the RGBA kernel before vendoring.
